treaty_name: Convention between the Government of the Republic of Slovenia and the Swiss Federal Council for the avoidance of double taxation with respect to taxes on income and on capital (1996, as amended 2012 and 2023)
eif_quote: FURS "Seznam veljavnih mednarodnih pogodb o izogibanju dvojnega obdavčevanja ... ki se uporabljajo v letu 2026" (Država | Objava | Začetek uporabe KIDO | Združeno besedilo | Začetek uporabe MLI): ŠVICA | MP, št. 15/97, | 1. 1. 1998 | | |
source_title: Uradni list RS – Mednarodne pogodbe 15/1997 (Convention), 5/2013 (Protocol 2012), 9/2023 (Protocol 2023); Slovenian and English texts

rates.article: Article 10(3)(a) as replaced by Protocol 2012 art. IV
rates.quote: Notwithstanding the provisions of paragraph 2, the Contracting State of which the company is a resident shall exempt from tax dividends paid by that company, if the beneficial owner of the dividends is: a) a company (other than a partnership) which is a resident of the other Contracting State and holds directly at least 25 per cent of the capital in the company paying the dividends;

rates.article: Article 10(2) as replaced by Protocol 2012 art. IV
rates.quote: However, such dividends may also be taxed in the Contracting State of which the company paying the dividends is a resident and according to the laws of that State, but if the beneficial owner of the dividends is a resident of the other Contracting State, the tax so charged shall not exceed 15 per cent of the gross amount of the dividends.

rates.article: Article 11(2) as replaced by Protocol 2012 art. V
rates.quote: However, such interest may also be taxed in the Contracting State in which it arises and according to the laws of that State, but if the beneficial owner of the interest is a resident of the other Contracting State, the tax so charged shall not exceed 5 per cent of the gross amount of the interest.

rates.article: Article 11(3)(f) as replaced by Protocol 2012 art. V
rates.quote: Notwithstanding the provisions of paragraph 2, interest arising in a Contracting State and paid to a resident of the other Contracting State who is the beneficial owner thereof shall be taxable only in that other State to the extent that such interest is paid ... f) by a company to a company of the other Contracting State where such company is affiliated with the company paying the interest by a direct minimum holding of 25 per cent in the capital or where both companies are held by a third company (being a resident of any Member State of European Union or of Switzerland) which has directly a minimum holding of 25 per cent, both in the capital of the first company and in the capital of the second company.

rates.article: Article 12(2) as replaced by Protocol 2012 art. VI
rates.quote: However, such royalties may also be taxed in the Contracting State in which they arise and according to the laws of that State, but if the beneficial owner of the royalties is a resident of the other Contracting State, the tax so charged shall not exceed 5 per cent of the gross amount of the royalties.

rates.article: Article 12(3) as replaced by Protocol 2012 art. VI
rates.quote: Notwithstanding paragraph 2, royalties paid by a company which is a resident of a Contracting State to a resident of the other Contracting State shall be taxable only in that other State if the beneficial owner is a company where such company is affiliated with the company paying the royalties by a direct minimum holding of 25 per cent in the capital or where both companies are held by a third company (being a resident of any Member State of European Union or of Switzerland) which has directly a minimum holding of 25 per cent, both in the capital of the first company and in the capital of the second company.

ppt.quote: Notwithstanding the other provisions of this Convention, a benefit under this Convention shall not be granted in respect of an item of income or capital if it is reasonable to conclude, having regard to all relevant facts and circumstances, that obtaining that benefit was one of the principal purposes of any arrangement or transaction that resulted directly or indirectly in that benefit, unless it is established that granting that benefit in these circumstances would be in accordance with the object and purpose of the relevant provisions of this Convention.

notes: Original convention (MP 15/97) applied from 1.1.1998 (5%/25% and 15% dividends, 5% interest, 5% royalties). Protocol 2012 (MP 5/13; EIF 2013-10-14 per merged data) replaced Arts. 10-12 with effect for WHT on amounts paid or credited on or after 1 January of the year following its entry into force -> 1.1.2014 (FURS: 1. 1. 2014). Current regime: dividends 15%, exempt at source for a company (other than partnership) holding directly >=25% (no holding period in text) and for pension schemes (not modelled); interest 5%, exempt for government/central-bank, export-credit, credit-sale, bank-to-bank (not modelled) and 25% affiliated-company interest (direct 25% holding or common 25% EU/Swiss parent); royalties 5%, exempt between 25% affiliated companies (same test). Protocol 2023 (MP 9/23; SIF: in force 16.10.2024, applicable from 1.1.2025) added Art. 27A PPT and a switch-over in Art. 23(2)(d); no rate changes. MLI does not cover this treaty (Switzerland does not list SI).
